note: M7.3. Eight agent questions with the tools that must appear, the tools that would be wrong, and the fewest hops that could do it. No exact sequence is pinned: several paths through six tools are legitimately correct. Lives under var/ because var/** is in the golden set's eval_exclude, which is the only place a question may be written down without becoming a literal match for itself in the corpus it is scored against.

questions.question: Find the recorded decision about combining two retrievers into one ranking, then read one of the memories it cites in full and tell me what that file does.
questions.notes: The cleanest dependency test in the set: hop 2 needs a memory id that only hop 1's evidence line can supply. The chain M7.1 could not walk at all and M7.2's follow-up fixed.

questions.question: There is a decision about what a chunk's character offsets index into. Find it, then open one of the files it used as evidence and say what that file asserts.
questions.notes: Same shape as the first but the decision is found by topic rather than by mechanism, so hop 1 can legitimately be a search.

questions.question: Locate the code that lets one background worker take a job without another taking the same one, then tell me what else in this corpus is structurally connected to it.
questions.notes: Answerable=false and the reason is data, not reasoning: entity extraction has covered ~13% of the corpus, so traverse_graph returns nothing for almost any seed. The first half is answerable and the second is not, which is exactly the case the taxonomy must not call an agent failure.

questions.question: Why is the embedding model the one it is, and what was rejected in its favour?
questions.notes: One hop, and it is in the set to check that the loop does not pad. A question a single tool answers should cost a single hop.

questions.question: Which of the assumptions recorded under my decisions were later found to be wrong, and what were they about?
questions.notes: Reachable in one hop because get_decisions renders assumptions with their verdicts, but a thorough agent may take two. Efficiency is capped at 1.0, so taking two is a cost rather than a failure.

questions.question: Which month has the most recorded activity, and what was being worked on during it?
questions.notes: No key facts: the answer depends on the corpus's own dates, and a fact list would have to be rewritten every time the corpus grows. Scored on tools, hops and termination.

questions.question: Was there ever a stretch where work on this stopped for a while, and if so when?
questions.notes: The honest answer on this corpus is that there is no such stretch, which is an answer rather than a failure. No key facts, because a correct reply contains no distinctive noun.

questions.question: Across the past several years, how has the balance between writing tests and writing documentation shifted in my work?
questions.notes: The corpus spans weeks, not years, and nothing records the distinction it asks about. The correct outcome is a refusal or a statement of absence; asserting a trend anyway is the WRONG_CONCLUSION this entry exists to catch.
